checks.source: Rawal G, Yadav S, Kumar R, Wani UR (2016). Ofloxacin Induced Angioedema: A Rare Adverse Drug Reaction. Journal of Clinical and Diagnostic Research.

source_fit_rows.source_population: 24-year-old woman in New Delhi, India prescribed outpatient antibiotic therapy for diarrhea ('loose motions') who subsequently developed drug-induced lip angioedema (case report)
source_fit_rows.family_population: 33-year-old Indian English speaker with 14 days of mild belly bloating and loose motions 4 times daily after returning from a camping trip
source_fit_rows.note: Both involve young-adult Indian English outpatients seeking treatment for 'loose motions' (used verbatim, matching core entry 'loose motions' in dialect_lexicon_20261109.json), adapted from clinician case-report prose focused on subsequent antibiotic angioedema to a first-person 14-day post-camping diarrhea presentation.
